text: Individualistic: Ger. individualistisch ; Fr. individualiste ; Ital. individualistico . (1) In sociology: applied to theories which advocate or imply INDIVIDUALISM (q.v.). ( J.M.B. ) (2) In ethics: applied to those theories which derive the moral ideal or standard from the nature -- desires or conscience -- of the individual man. All forms of EPICUREANISM, as well as the MORAL SENSE theory of ethics, and most forms of INTUITIONISM are thus individualistic (see those terms and ETHICAL THEORIES). The chief difficulty of such theories lies in bringing out the grounds and place of social duty. Cf. Sorley, Eth . of Nat ., chaps. ii-iv. ( W.R.S. )
